08 — Data and Database Management Checklist#

Review data ownership, schema design, migration safety, transactional correctness, data quality, and lifecycle management. This checklist covers the integrity and governance of information throughout its use; apply the separate Security, Legal, Reliability, and Performance checklists for their deeper controls.

Scope: Backend / API-specific. This file is one part of the 08_Data_and_DatabaseManagement.md checklist. Apply the domain-wide release gate across all applicable scope files; each checklist ID remains unique.

Review details#

  • Project / product:
  • Release / version / environment:
  • Scope and applicable jurisdictions / markets:
  • Database engines / storage platforms:
  • Critical data assets and data owners:
  • Reviewer / owner:
  • Review date:
  • Decision: Pending / Approved / Approved with documented exceptions / Blocked

How to use#

  1. Copy this template to a project-specific review; leave all checkboxes unchecked in the shared repository.
  2. Mark [x] only after verification from schema definitions, migration tests, quality metrics, data dictionaries, lifecycle policies, or other relevant evidence. Record failed items and documented N/A reasons in project records or issues keyed by DATA ID, not in this shared checklist.
  3. Apply storage-specific controls according to the actual data stores and interfaces. Relational constraints, transaction isolation, partitioning, and OpenAPI are not universal requirements for document, key-value, graph, or other stores.
  4. Review ## API Checks and ## Frontend Checks separately for each applicable product surface, with explicit N/A rationale where necessary.
  5. Revisit the checklist after material data-model changes, new integrations, data migrations, changed processing purposes, or updates to privacy/retention obligations. Consult qualified legal and privacy specialists for jurisdiction-specific obligations.

Data modeling and governance#

  • DATA-009 Use schema-level primary key, unique, foreign key, and check constraints for invariants that the chosen database can enforce.

  • DATA-016 Define tenant, organization, and ownership boundaries for shared tables, object storage, search indexes, and analytical datasets.

  • DATA-127 Use parameterized SQL or equivalent safe driver bindings for untrusted values, and allowlist structural query choices such as column names, table names, and sort directions; review dynamic SQL inside stored procedures and ORM queries.

  • DATA-128 Where RLS is used, test SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE (existing and resulting rows) and DELETE with real anonymous, member, tenant and admin roles; reject forged ownership/cross-tenant access and audit owner/service/BYPASSRLS-equivalent bypass.

  • DATA-129 Verify runtime, reporting, migration, and administrator database accounts have only required table, schema, function, and default privileges, and test denial of unauthorized direct database access.

  • DATA-141 Test pooled-connection reuse for leakage of tenant identity, row-security context, session variables, search paths, temporary objects, and transaction state between unrelated requests.

  • DATA-153 For encrypted database connections, verify certificate-chain and hostname validation, credential handling, and trusted proxy behavior rather than assuming transport encryption alone authenticates the destination.

  • DATA-001 Inventory authoritative data stores, major datasets, data products, and ownership boundaries across the system.

  • DATA-002 Assign a business owner and technical steward to each critical dataset and record their escalation contacts.

  • DATA-003 Document the purpose, intended consumers, sensitivity, and expected lifecycle of each important data category.

  • DATA-004 Identify the source of truth for each business entity and avoid conflicting writable replicas without defined reconciliation.

  • DATA-005 Model entities, relationships, identifiers, and cardinality in an up-to-date conceptual or logical schema.

  • DATA-006 Define stable primary keys and public identifiers with explicit uniqueness and lifecycle expectations where applicable.

  • DATA-007 Document the semantics, units, timezone, precision, and allowed values of important fields.

  • DATA-008 Define nullability, defaults, optionality, missing-value semantics, and field deprecation rules consistently.

  • DATA-010 Define ownership and accepted consequences of cascade, restrict, and soft-delete relationships rather than relying on defaults.

  • DATA-011 Choose normalization or deliberate denormalization based on measured access needs and consistency trade-offs.

  • DATA-012 Assess document, graph, time-series, key-value, or relational models against actual access patterns and integrity requirements.

  • DATA-013 Document event, audit, operational, analytical, and derived data separately so consumers do not treat derived copies as authoritative.

  • DATA-014 Map data flows across services, integrations, queues, analytics stores, caches, and external recipients.

  • DATA-015 Record classifications such as public, internal, confidential, or restricted, tied to real processing and access controls.

  • DATA-017 Document data lineage from source capture to processing, transformation, publication, and downstream consumption.

  • DATA-018 Establish change ownership and approval for material schema, data contract, and governance decisions.

  • DATA-019 Identify regulatory, contractual, or sector-specific handling obligations with the qualified legal or privacy owner.

  • DATA-020 Define discoverable data dictionaries and schema documentation with accountable maintenance responsibility.

  • DATA-124 For each business-critical workflow, specify acceptable database read consistency, acknowledged-write durability, and maximum staleness; test these guarantees under normal operation and failover.

  • DATA-125 Establish and exercise a database-provider exit or data-portability plan using a representative export and re-import that preserves identifiers, constraints, encodings, and dependent consumer mappings.

Database operations and migrations#

  • DATA-022 Apply schema changes through a consistent, automated or controlled deployment workflow rather than untracked manual updates.

  • DATA-026 Verify that application versions coexisting during deployment remain compatible with the intended transitional schema.

  • DATA-032 Detect schema drift between the expected migration history and actual deployed database definitions.

  • DATA-033 Use distinct, narrowly scoped database identities for applications, migration automation, and administrators.

  • DATA-035 Ensure database connection pool configuration, timeouts, and retry behavior are documented for expected load.

  • DATA-040 Ensure database versions, extensions, drivers, and client libraries have an owner and supported upgrade plan.

  • DATA-041 Test scheduled maintenance, failover, and database upgrades for client compatibility and connection recovery.

  • DATA-042 Review storage and database configuration for availability, durability, performance, and applicable access-control requirements.

  • DATA-130 Keep representative execution-plan and latency baselines for high-impact SQL queries across realistic table sizes, parameter values, and data skew; investigate regressions after schema, statistics, or engine changes.

  • DATA-131 Choose and benchmark composite, partial, expression, or covering indexes against actual predicates and sort orders where supported, measuring read gains against write amplification, storage, and maintenance costs.

  • DATA-132 Review index-usage statistics for redundant, duplicate, or consistently unused indexes and validate workload and rollback safety before removing an index.

  • DATA-133 Detect and correct N+1 database queries caused by ORM relations or resolver loops using representative list and nested-object workloads, rather than relying only on API request counts.

  • DATA-134 Benchmark deep pagination and large sort/filter workloads; use bounded queries and keyset or cursor techniques where appropriate to avoid high-offset scans and unstable ordering.

  • DATA-135 For partitioned data, test partition pruning, partition-boundary reads/writes, default-partition growth, and the safe expiry or detachment of old partitions under production-like data distributions.

  • DATA-136 For sharded databases, validate shard-key cardinality, skew, monotonic hot spots, query-routing efficiency, and resharding recovery plans against observed access patterns.

  • DATA-137 Monitor long-running and idle-open transactions, lock waits, deadlocks, and blocked writers with workload-specific thresholds, diagnostic attribution, and escalation ownership.

  • DATA-138 Set and exercise appropriate database statement, lock-wait, and idle-in-transaction time budgets, including cancellation and connection-pool behavior when those limits are reached.

  • DATA-140 Capacity-test aggregate database connection-pool limits across all service instances, background jobs, and tenants, reserving operational headroom and applying backpressure before exhausting server connections.

  • DATA-143 Where replication slots or log-based CDC are used, monitor lag, retained-log/WAL bytes, abandoned slots, and disk thresholds; define safe consumer recovery or retirement procedures.

  • DATA-144 For logical database replication, verify how DDL, indexes, privileges, sequence values, and incompatible column changes are synchronized and tested during cutovers rather than assuming data replication covers them.

  • DATA-148 Demonstrate point-in-time recovery to a selected timestamp or log position using a valid base backup and complete incremental/log chain; reconcile recovered business records with the agreed recovery objective.

  • DATA-149 Alert on failed, delayed, or missing transaction-log/WAL archiving and validate that backup retention never deletes a base or incremental dependency required for the promised recovery window.

  • DATA-150 For MVCC databases such as PostgreSQL, monitor vacuum or compaction backlog, long-lived snapshots, and transaction-ID age; verify anti-wraparound maintenance completes before write availability is threatened.

  • DATA-151 After bulk data changes or material shifts in column-value distributions, verify planner statistics and relevant multicolumn correlations are refreshed before accepting critical query performance.

  • DATA-152 Test protections against unbounded scans, expensive sorts, temporary-disk spill, and runaway database queries using representative adversarial but authorized workloads.

  • DATA-155 During long-running backfills or dual-read/dual-write transitions, test concurrent inserts, updates, and deletes for lost changes, reconciliation gaps, and safe restart at checkpoints.

  • DATA-021 Track schema definitions and migrations in version control, with reviewed ownership and change descriptions.

  • DATA-023 Test migrations against representative data volumes, versions, constraints, indexes, and realistic schema history.

  • DATA-024 Estimate and measure migration duration, lock impact, resource consumption, and required maintenance windows.

  • DATA-025 Use additive/expand-contract migration steps where compatible rolling releases or independent consumers require them.

  • DATA-027 Ensure required data backfills are restartable or safely resumable after partial completion.

  • DATA-028 Specify batching, checkpoints, and throttling for long-running updates to avoid exhausting transactions or production resources.

  • DATA-029 Test safe handling of preexisting invalid data before introducing stronger constraints or new required fields.

  • DATA-030 Define an explicit strategy for changes that cannot be rolled back, including forward remediation or restoration plans.

  • DATA-031 Record migration ordering, application dependencies, ownership, and go/no-go decision points.

  • DATA-034 Require appropriate approval and auditability for production data fixes, destructive migrations, and privileged operations.

  • DATA-036 Monitor query execution plans and slow queries before introducing or removing performance-critical indexes.

  • DATA-037 Measure index creation or rebuild impact and choose online/concurrent methods when supported and warranted.

  • DATA-038 Review storage growth, vacuum/compaction, maintenance tasks, partitioning, and capacity thresholds for the selected engine.

  • DATA-039 Document replica topology, consistency/lag behavior, and rules for sending read and write traffic where replicas are used.

Integrity and quality#

  • DATA-050 Use optimistic locking, version numbers, database locking, or equivalent controls where concurrent edits would cause data loss.

  • DATA-064 Retest critical integrity guarantees after schema changes, new integrations, and database engine upgrades.

  • DATA-139 For deadlock or serialization failures, test bounded retries of the complete transaction with backoff and no repeated irreversible side effects; distinguish retryable errors from permanent constraint failures.

  • DATA-142 When a connection drops or times out near commit, reconcile the authoritative transaction outcome before repeating a write so uncertain success does not cause duplicate or missing effects.

  • DATA-145 Test change-data-capture initial snapshot-to-stream handoff, resume-position persistence, duplicate delivery, missing event detection, and out-of-order replay using representative updates and deletes.

  • DATA-146 Where database changes publish events, verify that state updates and durable outbox records commit atomically, and that downstream publication/consumption can recover without losing or duplicating business effects.

  • DATA-147 For outbox or CDC consumers, verify event identifiers, per-entity ordering assumptions, retry/dead-letter handling, and idempotent reprocessing after a consumer outage.

  • DATA-154 For replica-backed reads, test freshness thresholds and read-after-write routing during replica lag or failover so workflows requiring current values do not silently consume stale results.

  • DATA-043 Define required field completeness, uniqueness, validity, consistency, accuracy, and freshness checks for critical datasets.

  • DATA-045 Validate schema types, ranges, formats, references, and expected enumerations before accepting new data.

  • DATA-046 Establish rules for duplicate detection, entity identity resolution, and permitted legitimate duplicates.

  • DATA-047 Define transaction boundaries for multi-step operations that must commit or fail as one unit.

  • DATA-048 Choose transaction isolation and concurrency controls that preserve required invariants under simultaneous writes.

  • DATA-049 Test lost-update, write-conflict, double-submit, and transaction retry scenarios on high-risk workflows.

  • DATA-051 Test that retries, repeated messages, and redelivered events cannot duplicate committed effects beyond the defined contract.

  • DATA-052 Define validation and reconciliation rules between source records, derived tables, replicas, and downstream consumers.

  • DATA-053 Measure data freshness and replication or processing lag where consumers depend on timely updates.

  • DATA-054 Specify handling for missing, stale, late, out-of-order, or malformed data in scheduled and streaming pipelines.

  • DATA-055 Add automated data-quality checks to ingestion and transformation pipelines with ownership for failures.

  • DATA-056 Define quarantine, rejection, correction, and replay behavior for invalid records without silently discarding them.

  • DATA-057 Reconcile record counts, checksums, totals, or domain-level invariants after migrations and bulk imports.

  • DATA-058 Ensure numerical precision and rounding rules are appropriate for financial, scientific, and other exact-value fields.

  • DATA-059 Verify character encoding, locale-aware comparisons, case rules, and timezone conversion do not corrupt meaning.

  • DATA-060 Check that tenant identifiers and access boundaries are preserved in joins, exports, transformations, and background jobs.

  • DATA-061 Capture auditable changes to regulated or high-impact data with sufficient context without logging protected secrets unnecessarily.

  • DATA-062 Investigate and track failed quality assertions with severity, data owner, affected scope, and remediation status.

  • DATA-063 Monitor for unexpected schema changes and data distributions that indicate upstream defects.

Retention and lifecycle#

  • DATA-065 Inventory personal, sensitive, transactional, audit, analytical, temporary, and derived data with their retention owners.
  • DATA-066 Document the purpose and applicable contractual, regulatory, or business justification for each retention period.
  • DATA-067 Define retention start events and durations precisely, including time zones, inactivity, account closure, or other triggers.
  • DATA-068 Identify data that must not be retained after its processing purpose ends, subject to applicable exceptions and obligations.
  • DATA-069 Document circumstances requiring retention holds, disputes, investigations, or other authorized suspensions of deletion.
  • DATA-070 Define archival tiers, data access limits, and permitted downstream uses for information kept beyond active operation.
  • DATA-071 Automate expiry, archive, anonymization, or deletion workflows where appropriate, with observable completion signals.
  • DATA-072 Verify deletion affects derived stores, search indexes, analytics replicas, exports, and caches to the extent required.
  • DATA-073 Account for backup retention and delayed erasure processes under the applicable legal framework and documented policy.
  • DATA-074 Ensure soft-delete records, tombstones, and archived copies have clear lifecycle and access semantics.
  • DATA-075 Provide processes to handle valid user or customer access, correction, portability, and erasure requests where legally applicable.
  • DATA-076 Distinguish pseudonymization from irreversible anonymization in internal data classification and deletion claims.
  • DATA-077 Verify anonymization or aggregation prevents reasonable reidentification before treating resulting datasets as anonymous.
  • DATA-078 Control access and log authorized retrieval of archived or previously restricted data.
  • DATA-079 Identify minimum necessary data fields and avoid collecting additional attributes only for speculative future use.
  • DATA-080 Document external recipients and processors that must receive corrections, deletion requests, or retention changes where required.
  • DATA-081 Define purge/reconciliation checks that detect orphaned records and expired data in secondary systems.
  • DATA-082 Check that temporary uploads, export files, failed jobs, and staging datasets do not remain indefinitely.
  • DATA-083 Define secure media disposal, credential destruction, and device-level data sanitization when hardware or storage is retired.
  • DATA-084 Review retention schedules and lifecycle controls periodically as products, data use, and obligations change.
  • DATA-126 Review data residency and authorized cross-border transfer boundaries for database replicas, backups, snapshots, analytics copies, and disaster-recovery environments before provisioning them.

API Checks#

  • DATA-085 Define the canonical meaning and authoritative source of every critical field exposed by an API.
  • DATA-086 Publish stable request and response schemas with explicit field types, nullability, units, and identifier semantics.
  • DATA-087 Validate required fields, ranges, enum values, and nested structures at trusted API boundaries.
  • DATA-088 Check that errors for invalid data identify affected fields without disclosing protected internal data.
  • DATA-089 Enforce tenant, role, and object ownership boundaries for reads, writes, bulk operations, exports, and data searches.
  • DATA-090 Prevent mass assignment or unintended field updates by limiting writable fields to the approved contract.
  • DATA-091 Document idempotency and deduplication requirements for write operations that may be retried.
  • DATA-092 Define concurrency behavior for edits, including version preconditions, conflict responses, and retry guidance.
  • DATA-093 Ensure transaction semantics are documented when one API call changes multiple related records.
  • DATA-094 Specify pagination and filtering rules that provide stable identity and predictable results across changes.
  • DATA-095 Document read-after-write consistency, stale replica behavior, and expected freshness for important endpoints.
  • DATA-096 Treat schema evolution and data migration as API compatibility concerns; test old and new clients during rollout.
  • DATA-097 Make bulk imports, exports, and background jobs resumable or observable when partial failure is possible.
  • DATA-098 Validate API-supplied timestamps, decimal values, localization-sensitive fields, and encoding round trips.
  • DATA-099 Ensure sensitive fields are redacted or omitted from logs, API errors, and traces while retaining useful diagnostic context.
  • DATA-100 Define rate limits, quotas, and payload-size constraints for expensive data operations.
  • DATA-101 Ensure data deletion, correction, and export APIs propagate required lifecycle actions to dependent stores.
  • DATA-102 Test API responses for missing data, duplicates, concurrent updates, stale caches, and data-integrity failures.
  • DATA-103 Document consumers and deprecation plans before modifying field semantics or removing stored data they depend on.

Release gate#

  • Critical datasets have identified owners, documented data definitions, authoritative sources, and appropriate access/classification boundaries.
  • Schema and migration changes have been reviewed and tested against realistic data volumes and compatible application versions, with a credible path to recovery or remediation.
  • Business-critical invariants, transaction and concurrency guarantees, and data-quality checks have been validated; material discrepancies are reconciled or have accepted remediation plans.
  • Data retention, deletion, and archival controls have documented purposes and responsible owners, including relevant downstream and derived data copies.
  • API and frontend data contracts are consistent with authoritative semantics and remain compatible with the proposed release, where those interfaces exist.
  • Unresolved integrity, schema-change, or lifecycle risks have a named owner, priority, deadline, and authorized disposition recorded outside this shared template.

Domain-specific approval rule: Do not approve a release when critical records can be corrupted or silently lost, required migrations lack a safe plan, authoritative data ownership is unresolved, or significant retention and lifecycle risks remain unaccepted. Passing this review does not establish privacy-law compliance, database recoverability, or security certification.

Trusted references and scope#

The following primary sources inform these practical verification questions. The checks are not direct quotations of standards and do not imply that one data architecture is universally required.

  • PostgreSQL — Constraints — database-level uniqueness, checks, keys, and referential integrity.
  • PostgreSQL — Concurrency Control — transaction isolation, locking, and consistency under concurrent access.
  • PostgreSQL — Modifying Tables — schema evolution and constraint changes.
  • PostgreSQL — ALTER TABLE — schema changes, lock behavior, and constraints in live databases.
  • Microsoft Azure Well-Architected — Data platform considerations — governance, consistency, and schema evolution.
  • Microsoft Azure Well-Architected — Partitioning data — partition management, consistency, and lifecycle implications.
  • AWS Well-Architected — Data classification — classifications and related data protection/lifecycle decisions.
  • AWS Well-Architected — Data lifecycle management — handling, retention, transformation, and disposal policy.
  • AWS Well-Architected — Back up data — recovery prerequisites for critical data and configurations.
  • UK ICO — Storage limitation — personal-data retention and erasure considerations where applicable; guidance is under review.
  • OpenAPI Specification — machine-readable API data contracts when applicable.
  • OWASP — SQL Injection Prevention Cheat Sheet — parameterized queries and safe query structures.
  • PostgreSQL — Row Security Policies — isolation and privileged bypass considerations.
  • PostgreSQL — Indexes — index design, types, usage and maintenance costs.
  • PostgreSQL — EXPLAIN — query plan instrumentation and regressions.
  • PostgreSQL — Client Connection Defaults — query, lock, and idle-transaction timeouts.
  • PostgreSQL — Routine Vacuuming — long-lived snapshots and transaction-ID aging.
  • PostgreSQL — Planner Statistics — selectivity and multicolumn statistics.
  • PostgreSQL — Monitoring Statistics — database performance and replication monitoring.
  • PostgreSQL — Logical Replication Restrictions — limitations of replicated DDL and sequences.
  • PostgreSQL — Continuous Archiving and PITR — WAL retention, base backups, and point-in-time recovery.
  • MongoDB — Choose a Shard Key — distributed data placement, skew and hot keys.
  • Debezium — Outbox Event Router — atomic event creation and CDC consumers.
  • Microsoft Azure — Hybrid architecture considerations — portability, residency constraints, and disaster recovery planning.

Applicability: PostgreSQL-specific constraints and transaction behavior apply only to PostgreSQL or as illustrative relational concepts; verify equivalent capabilities for other engines. The UK ICO source is relevant only where the applicable data-protection framework requires it and is currently under review; do not apply UK-specific duties automatically to other jurisdictions. This checklist does not replace qualified legal, security, or data-architecture review.

Source review date: 2026-11-12.

Suggested testing tools#

Choose tools appropriate to the project's stack and risks; automation supports evidence but does not approve the checklist.

  • Test focus: migrations, constraints, permissions, data integrity, rollback, and concurrent writes; include API and service behavior where applicable.
  • Cross-stack: pgTAP + Testcontainers.
  • Python: testcontainers-python + Pandera + pytest; for pytest-based suites, run python -m pytest -q.
  • TypeScript: Testcontainers + Vitest; for Vitest-based suites, run npx vitest run (or npx playwright test for E2E).
  • JavaScript: Testcontainers + Jest; for Jest-based suites, run npx jest --ci (or npx playwright test for E2E).
  • Evidence: Save tool versions, configuration, test environment, fixtures, results, and links in project-specific review records using the existing checklist IDs. Expert review remains necessary where relevant.

Suggested AI skills for verification#

These are optional agent review aids, not automated passes or release approval. Each linked repository had at least 1,000 GitHub stars when checked on 2026-11-12; counts are per repository, not per skill, and do not indicate security or correctness.

  • data-quality-frameworks — Evaluate integrity and data-quality checks (wshobson/agents, 42,437 repo stars).
  • database-migration — Review schema changes and rollback risks (wshobson/agents, 42,437 repo stars).
  • property-based-testing — Find integrity and transaction edge cases (trailofbits/skills, 8,150 repo stars).

How to check: In a project-specific copy, have the agent audit the backend / API scope and map findings to this file's existing checklist IDs, with code/configuration references, reproducible test results, failed or inapplicable cases, and uncertainties. Independently verify findings; keep shared template boxes unchecked and retain human approval requirements.

Before use: Read the skill's SKILL.md, referenced scripts, license, and requested tool permissions. Only execute vetted skills with appropriate access in a controlled environment.

Important warning: reference only#

⚠️ Reference only — not a definitive or exhaustive checklist. This template is a starting point for review, not the ultimate authority or a guarantee of project safety, quality, regulatory compliance, accessibility, security, or launch readiness.

Use project-specific judgment and independent verification. Requirements and risks evolve and differ by project, technology, and jurisdiction. Adapt the checks, consult current authoritative sources, perform relevant tests, and obtain qualified specialist review or approval when appropriate. Checking every box does not replace these steps.

Reference, not a certification. Check applicability, verify important claims against current primary sources, and seek expert review where necessary. Suggest an improvement.
